finding.claim: The /logo endpoint sends an HTTP GET to an attacker-chosen URL. The only check is a substring match for 'example.io', so the URL can point at internal or cloud-metadata addresses. The response body is returned to the attacker, making this a full-response SSRF.
finding.source: main.go:31 - r.FormValue("logo"), an unauthenticated query parameter. The server listens on :8081 on all interfaces (main.go:44).
finding.sink: main.go:36 - http.Get(raw) using the default client, which follows redirects and has no host or IP restriction.

trace.note: raw is read directly from the attacker-controlled 'logo' query parameter
strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") matches anywhere in the string, including the query or path, so it does not validate the host
http.Get(raw) issues a request to the host named in raw
defer resp.Body.Close() panics when Get fails and resp is nil. The dropped connection can serve as a port-open oracle for internal hosts
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) returns the internal response body to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: (1) Substring check 'example.io' at main.go:32: bypassed by placing 'example.io' in the query or path, e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?example.io. (2) Scheme: net/http only supports http and https, so file:// and similar schemes are rejected, but http and https are allowed. (3) Redirects: the default client follows up to 10, so a redirect from an allowed host to an internal host is not blocked. (4) No private, loopback, or link-local IP blocking at dial time. (5) No authentication on the endpoint. Payloads were not executed; the finding is based on reading the code.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is the substring match `strings.Contains(raw, "example.io")` at main.go:32, which does not validate the parsed host and is not a closing guard. No scheme, host-set, or IP restriction exists anywhere on the path, and the default client at main.go:36 follows redirects.
verdict.reason: The `logo` parameter is read unauthenticated at main.go:31 from a server listening on all interfaces (main.go:44), passes only the substring check at main.go:32, and is fetched with `http.Get(raw)` at main.go:36 with the body copied back to the client at main.go:38, so this is a full-response SSRF. The defer at main.go:37 does panic on a failed request because `resp` is nil, as the candidate says, but that does not affect the verdict.
